AboutPage.metaDescription: Apercura publishes a free, factual page for every health practitioner registered in France, built from public open data.
AboutPage.title: About Apercura
AboutPage.lead: An open directory of every health practitioner in France, and a free booking tool for those who want one.

what.heading: What Apercura does
body: Apercura publishes a page for every doctor, dentist and midwife registered in France, built from the national register of health professionals and other public open data.

Patients find any practitioner, not only those who pay a platform. Practitioners can claim their page for free, check it and complete it. Free online booking, without a patient account, will open later.

principles.heading: Principles
list: Every practitioner is listed the same way, whether or not they use Apercura.
Factual information only: no ratings, no reviews, no ads and no paid ranking.
Free for practitioners and patients, with no subscription and no commission.
Each page shows where its facts come from and when they were last updated.
Minimal data, collected for a stated purpose and deleted on schedule.

how.heading: Where the pages come from
body: Pages are generated each week from the Annuaire Santé of the Agence du numérique en santé, the FINESS register of establishments and the Assurance Maladie directory. The data page lists every source, its licence and its date.

who.heading: Who runs Apercura
body: Apercura is a public-interest project. It is not a government service and is not affiliated with the Assurance Maladie, the Ordres or the Agence du numérique en santé.

OpenSourcePage.metaDescription: The full source code of Apercura is public under the AGPL-3.0 licence. Read it, audit it, or run the whole platform yourself.
OpenSourcePage.title: The code is public.
OpenSourcePage.lead: Every line of Apercura is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence: you can read it, audit it and run the whole platform yourself.

licence.heading: AGPL-3.0 licence
body: The AGPL-3.0 is a free software licence. Anyone may use, study, modify and share the code. Whoever offers a modified version as an online service must publish their changes under the same licence.

rules.heading: Which practitioners have a page
body: A practitioner has a public page when the register lists them with at least one activity open to patients (a practice, a health centre or a hospital) at an address. People without a fixed place of practice keep a record they can claim, but no public page.
Pages show facts only, in a neutral order: there are no ratings, no reviews and no paid ranking.

correct.heading: Correcting an error
body: Most facts come from registers kept by others, so the lasting fix is made at the source. The page follows at the next weekly import.
list: Name, profession, specialty, place of practice and phone: the practitioner updates their registration with their Ordre (or the body that registered them in the RPPS).
Agreement sector, OPTAM and Carte Vitale: they come from the Assurance Maladie directory (ameli.fr).
Name and address of an establishment: they come from the FINESS register, kept by the regional health agencies.
Practitioners will also be able to claim their page from the practitioners’ area, then complete it and correct what is shown.
correct.formTitle: The error report form is not open yet
correct.formBody: It will open on this page with practitioner accounts. Until then, the corrections above are the way to fix a page.

remove.heading: Objecting to a page
body: Under article 21 of the GDPR, a practitioner can object to the publication of their page. Apercura publishes the directory on the basis of a legitimate interest: informing the public from public data.

An unclaimed page will be hidden as soon as the request is received, then deleted after a light check of the request. A claimed page can be removed by its holder at any time. Once removed, a page does not come back with the next import.

AccessibilityPage.metaDescription: Accessibility statement of Apercura (draft): compliance status with RGAA 4.1, test methods, how to report a problem and your recourse.
AccessibilityPage.title: Accessibility
AccessibilityPage.lead: Apercura is designed for everyone, including older and low-vision people. This draft statement says where it stands.

commitment.heading: Commitment
body: Apercura aims to comply with the French accessibility framework RGAA 4.1 and with WCAG 2.2 level AA on every page.
Patient pages use body text of at least 18 px, targets of at least 44 px, visible focus, and nothing conveyed by colour alone.

status.heading: Compliance status
body: Apercura has not been audited against RGAA 4.1 yet. Until an audit is published, the site is considered not compliant. A full audit is planned before launch.

tests.heading: How the pages are tested
list: Automated checks with axe-core on every type of page, in each release.
Keyboard-only checks of search and navigation.
Manual checks with the VoiceOver and NVDA screen readers are planned with the audit.

technologies.heading: Technologies used
body: HTML, CSS, WAI-ARIA and JavaScript. Search and the directory pages also work without JavaScript.

feedback.heading: Reporting a problem
body: If you cannot access a content or a service, tell us so we can provide an alternative or fix the page.

recourse.heading: Recourse
body: If you reported a problem and did not get a satisfactory answer, you can contact the Défenseur des droits.
list: Online form of the Défenseur des droits
Post (free, no stamp): Défenseur des droits, Libre réponse 71120, 75342 Paris CEDEX 07

PrivacyPage.metaDescription: How Apercura processes personal data: directory data from public registers, no patient data yet, no trackers, and your rights.
PrivacyPage.title: Privacy
PrivacyPage.lead: Apercura collects as little as it can. This draft explains what is processed, why, and how to exercise your rights.

roles.heading: Who is responsible
body: For the public directory, Apercura is the data controller. For online bookings, once they open, Apercura will process data on behalf of each practitioner, under a processing agreement included in the practitioners’ terms.

practitioners.heading: Data about practitioners
body: Directory pages show facts from public registers: name, profession, specialties, places of practice, published phone numbers and agreement sector. Each page names its sources and the date of its last update.

The legal basis is a legitimate interest: informing the public from public data. Practitioners are not informed one by one, which would be a disproportionate effort (article 14.5.b of the GDPR); the data page and a notice on each page inform them instead.
Every practitioner can object to the publication of their page.

patients.heading: Data about patients
body: Online booking is not open yet: Apercura does not collect any patient data today. When booking opens, it will ask only for what the practitioner needs, encrypt it at the application level and delete it on schedule (90 days after the appointment by default).

cookies.heading: Cookies and trackers
body: Apercura uses no advertising or audience cookies and no trackers. Only cookies strictly needed for the service may be set, so no consent banner is needed.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask to access, correct or erase data about you, and object to its processing. If you think your rights are not respected, you can file a complaint with the CNIL.

TermsPage.metaDescription: Terms of use of Apercura (draft): a free, factual directory of health practitioners in France.
TermsPage.title: Terms of use
TermsPage.lead: These draft terms describe the service as it is today. They will be completed and reviewed before launch.

service.heading: The service
body: Apercura is a free directory of health practitioners registered in France, built from public open data. Using it requires no account.

content.heading: What the pages contain
body: Pages show factual information from public registers, in a neutral order. They carry no ratings, no reviews, no ads and no paid ranking.
The information can contain errors or be out of date: check it with the practitioner before travelling. Each page says how to report an error.

health.heading: Not medical advice
body: Apercura gives no medical advice and is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 15 (SAMU) or 112.

practitioners.heading: For practitioners
body: Claiming a page will be free and will require proof of identity. A practitioner who claims a page is responsible for the information they add to it, which must stay factual, as the codes of medical ethics require.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. Directory data is reused under the Licence Ouverte 2.0.

manage.missingBody: Open the link from your confirmation email again. If you copied it, make sure you copied all of it.
manage.invalidBody: The appointment may have been erased after its date, or the link was not copied in full. For any question, contact the practice.
manage.errorBody: Your appointment could not be loaded. Check your connection, then try again.

confirmEmail.body: The practice typed this address for you. Confirm that it is yours to receive reminders and changes by email.
confirmEmail.done: Thank you: your address is confirmed.

manage.cancelConfirmBody: The time will be offered to other patients. This cannot be undone.
manage.cancelled: Your appointment is cancelled. A confirmation email is on its way.

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.lead: Your practitioner space: your page, your agenda, your team.
signIn.asideFactor: Every account that can reach appointments needs a second factor: a code from an authenticator app or a passkey.
signIn.asidePasskey: A passkey is kept on your phone or computer and unlocked with your fingerprint, face or PIN.
signIn.passkeyHint: No password needed: your device confirms it is you.
signIn.totpLead: Open your authenticator app and enter the 6-digit code shown for Apercura.
signIn.backupLead: Each backup code works once. You received them when you set up your authenticator app.

signUp.title: Create an account
signUp.lead: Free for practitioners and their assistants.
signUp.asideSteps: Three steps: create the account, confirm your email address, then set up a second factor.
signUp.asideFree: Creating an account does not change any public page. Claiming your page comes next.
signUp.name: First and last name
signUp.emailHint: We send a confirmation link to this address.
signUp.passwordHint: At least {min} characters. A long sentence is easy to remember.
signUp.sentTitle: We sent a confirmation link to {email}.
signUp.sentBody: Open the email and follow the link within an hour. Then sign in to set up your second factor.
signUp.sentHint: Nothing after a few minutes? Check your spam folder, or sign in: we will send a new link.

verifyEmail.title: Email confirmation
verifyEmail.successBody: Sign in with your password to set up your second factor.
verifyEmail.errorBody: It may have expired or been used already. Sign in: we will send you a new link.

challenge.title: Confirm it is you
challenge.lead: Your account has a second factor: use it to open your space.
challenge.aside: Your password alone is not enough to reach appointments.
challenge.passkeyLead: Your device asks for your fingerprint, face or PIN.
challenge.otherHeading: Not you, or no access to your factor?
challenge.otherLead: Sign out. Recovering an account means verifying your identity again.

security.title: Security
security.lead: How you sign in, and where you are signed in.
security.enrolLead: One last step before your space: set up a second factor.
security.enrolTitle: Choose a second factor to continue
security.enrolBody: Apercura asks every account that can reach appointments for one. An authenticator app or a passkey both work; you can add the other later.

totp.heading: Authenticator app
totp.lead: An app on your phone (for example FreeOTP, Aegis or Google Authenticator) shows a new 6-digit code every 30 seconds.
totp.enabledTitle: The authenticator app is set up.
totp.enabledBody: You will be asked for a code each time you sign in with your password.
totp.scanLead: In your authenticator app, add an account and scan this code. If you cannot scan it, type the setup key.
totp.qrLabel: QR code to add Apercura to your authenticator app
totp.codesLead: If you lose your phone, each of these codes lets you sign in once. Print them or store them in a password manager; they are shown only now.
totp.confirmHeading: 3. Enter the code shown by the app
totp.passwordHint: We ask for it again before changing how you sign in.

passkeys.heading: Passkeys
passkeys.lead: A passkey stays on your phone, computer or security key and is unlocked with your fingerprint, face or PIN. Nothing to type, nothing to steal.
passkeys.name: Name

sessions.heading: Where you are signed in
sessions.lead: A session ends after 12 hours without use. Sign out any session you do not recognise.
sessions.everywhereHint: Lost a device or shared your password? Sign out of every session, this one included.

app.title: Your space
app.emptyBody: Your practice appears here once you have claimed your page. Claiming is not open yet; your account is ready for it.
app.securityBody: Your account is protected by a second factor. Manage your authenticator app, passkeys and sessions.

email.footer: Apercura: the open directory of health practitioners in France. Free and open source.

verify.subject: Confirm your email address
verify.preview: Confirm your email address to finish creating your Apercura account.
verify.title: Confirm your email address
verify.body: You have just created an Apercura account. Confirm that this address is yours to continue.
verify.fallback: If the button does not work, copy this link into your browser:
verify.expiry: The link works for one hour.
verify.ignore: You did not create this account? Ignore this email: nothing will happen.
